newsitem.title: UK: Analysts dismiss reports of MEPC/Hammerson merger.
newsitem.headline: Analysts dismiss reports of MEPC/Hammerson merger.

text.p: Renewed reports of a bid for British property company MEPC Plc by its smaller rival Hammerson Plc were dismissed out of hand by property analysts on Friday.
"I think its clearly rubbish," an analyst at one European investment bank told Reuters.
The Daily Mail newspaper said a rise in MEPC's share price on Thursday was the result of speculation about an agreed merger.

The analyst, who declined to be named, said a restriction on various shareholding institutions, imposed when the two groups were in talks about a merger last month, had been lifted. This meant an agreed merger was not on the cards, he added.

"Nothing is going to happen while MEPC's share price is above its NAV (net asset value)," the analyst said. He estimated the firm's NAV at 460 pence, while the shares were quoted at 491.5 pence at 1216 GMT.
This represented a premium to NAV, which while below the sector average of 13 percent, would not allow Hammerson to make an offer for MEPC.
Another analyst said an agreed merger was "highly unlikely". "I don't think Hammerson's shareholders would want it," he said, adding that the smaller firm could not make a cash bid.

"Unless there is a shake-out in property (share) prices, which we don't expect, we would not expect anything for at least six months," the first analyst said. For Hammerson to make a hostile bid for MEPC, the former's premium to asset value would have to be at least 25 percent, he added.
Hammerson's shares were trading at 466 pence at 1215 GMT, up 3.5 pence on the day.
